page.layout: One column of running text, with Arabic and Greek inline. Below the text a verse line in Arabic, then the catchword at the right and the signature at the left. No margin notes. The right side of the page is empty.

main_text.p: servus, se quidem ipsum quasi jamjam profecturum reliquisse, profectus autem esset necne, se re vera nescire, nec pronuntiare velle, cum qui de absentibus loquatur, facile mentiri possit. Quo] responso & mendacium fugit servus, & domino suo pignum, quo certabatur, lucratus est. Adhibetur ergo cum quis de rebus de quibus nihil comperti habeat, loqui re-cuser, ne forsan quod falsum est dicere cogatur.

Prov. 60. الحديث ذو شجون Narratio (sermo) res carcerum est. lege ذو شجون i. e. quid modos, vel vias seu ramos habens, scil. [illegible, ~9 letters] & παυσμὸς[?] ita ut aliud ex alio sequatur, & inter loquendum, seu in sermonis progressu exsistat. شجون explicante authore AlKamusi inter alia significat, الغصن المشتبك ramum implexum, & rei cujusvis divortia, qui & hoc proverbium citans ذو شجون per Species seu modos & scopos, explicat, Alfaubar. Sermo est ذو شجون i.e. Pars ejus partem ingreditur, seu ita inter se cohaerent ejus partes, ut aliud ex alio inferatur المثل في الحديث يستشهد به غيره Dicitur de sermone quando unum aliud in memoriam revocat, seu quando unius occasione alterius fit mentio. Ex eâdem historiâ alterius etiam est proverbii origo, quod legit D. Erpenius سيف العدل Anticipavit justitiam ensis. Legendum autem est العذل Reprehensionem. sero scil. illum reprehenderunt ob cædem mense sacro patratam, re jam peractâ, quæ infectâ reddi non potuit. Alludit ad hoc proverbium Tograius in isto versu
ان كان ينفع شي في ثبادهم[?]

page.notes: Long s was read as f in the scan and is written as s. The Greek phrase after "scil." is too faint to read and is marked illegible. The Arabic verse line and the catchword "علي" are doubtful. The stray "]" after "Quo" and after "Prov. 60." may be printed marks and are kept as printed. The Arabic word "العذل" is printed in the text as the source for "Reprehensionem" and is copied as seen.
